'''坤'''（こん）は[[八卦]]の一つ。卦の形は[[画像:Kon.png]]であり、三爻すべてが[[陰陽|陰]]で構成される。または[[六十四卦]]の一つであり、坤為地。坤上坤下で構成される。
== 八卦 == 地・順・牛・腹・母などを象徴する。[[方位]]としては西南、すなわち'''ひつじさる'''を示す。
[[Category:易|こん]]

== 卦象 == 地・順・牛・腹・母・祖母·婦徳・胃・右肩·腹·補佐役・鈍重・大衆・迷いなどを象徴する。[[方位]]としては[[西南]]、すなわち[[地支]]の[[未]]と[[申]]の間、'''ひつじさる'''を示す。
[[納甲]]では[[乙]]、[[五行思想|五行]]の[[木]]、[[五方]]の[[東]]、または[[癸]]、[[五行思想|五行]]の[[水]]、[[五方]]の[[北]]に当てられる。
== 先天図 == 伏羲先天八卦における次序は八であり、方位は四正卦の一つで[[北]]に配される。[[陰陽]]消息は陰が極まったところである。

{{otheruses|Nine Stars of Divination|Nine Stars in Indian Astronomy|Nine Luminaries}} {{Cite source|date=December 2018}} {{color}} '''Nine Stars''' ({{ill|Nine Stars|ja|九星}}, Kyūsei) is a form of [[folk belief]] originating from ancient [[China]], consisting of nine stars: '''First White''', '''Second Black''', '''Third Blue''', '''Fourth Green''', '''Fifth Yellow''', '''Sixth White''', '''Seventh Red''', '''Eighth White''', and '''Ninth Purple'''.
The term "Nine Stars" can refer to several systems, and the one described here is specifically referred to as the "Purple White Nine Stars" or "Seven Colored Stars."
== Origin == The Nine Stars system originates from the following {{ill|magic square|ja|魔方陣}}:
{| class="wikitable" |- |Four||Nine||Two |- |Three||Five||Seven |- |Eight||One||Six |}
In this magic square, the sum of any row, column, or diagonal equals 15. It uses the numbers 1 through 9 exactly once in a 3×3 grid. This configuration, called the '''Later Heaven Arrangement''' ({{ill|Later Heaven Arrangement|ja|後天定位盤}}), is the only one of its kind, excluding rotations and reflections. These numbers are paired with seven colors (white, black, blue, green, yellow, red, and purple), the {{ill|five elements|ja|五行思想}} ({{ill|wood|ja|木}}, {{ill|fire|ja|火}}, {{ill|earth|ja|土}}, {{ill|metal|ja|金}}, and {{ill|water|ja|水}}), the {{ill|ten heavenly stems|ja|十干}}, the {{ill|twelve earthly branches|ja|十二支}}, and the {{ill|eight trigrams|ja|八卦}} of {{ill|I Ching|ja|易経}}. When these numbers shift positions, interpretations are added to form the "Nine Stars."
According to legend, {{ill|Yu the Great|ja|禹}}, founder of the {{ill|Xia Dynasty|ja|夏王朝}}, conceived this magic square when he encountered a sacred turtle emerging from the {{ill|Luo River|ja|洛水}}. This magic square is called the "Writing of the Luo" ({{ill|Luo Writing|ja|洛書}}), one of the {{ill|River Chart and Luo Writing|ja|河図洛書}}.
== The Nine Stars == In Japanese {{ill|Onmyōdō|ja|陰陽道}}, the following table associates the Nine Stars with the {{ill|five elements|ja|五行思想}}, {{ill|directions|ja|方位}}, {{ill|eight trigrams|ja|八卦}}, and colors, forming the '''Nine Stars Chart''' used to predict {{ill|fortune|ja|運勢}} and the {{ill|auspiciousness|ja|吉凶}} of directions based on a person's birth year.
{| class="wikitable" |- ! Star ! Reading ! Five Element ! Direction ! Eight Trigram ! Color |- ! {{ill|First White Water Star|ja|一白水星}} | Ippaku Suisei | Water | {{ill|North|ja|北}} | {{ill|Kan|ja|坎}} | style="background:white;"| White |- ! {{ill|Second Black Earth Star|ja|二黒土星}} | Jikoku Dosei | Earth | Southwest | {{ill|Kun|ja|坤}} | style="background:black;color:white;"| Black |- ! {{ill|Third Blue Wood Star|ja|三碧木星}} | Sanpeki Mokusei | Wood | {{ill|East|ja|東}} | {{ill|Zhen|ja|震}} | style="background:blue;color:white;"| Blue |- ! {{ill|Fourth Green Wood Star|ja|四緑木星}} | Shiroku Mokusei | Wood | Southeast | {{ill|Xun|ja|巽}} | style="background:green;color:white;"| Green |- ! {{ill|Fifth Yellow Earth Star|ja|五黄土星}} | Goō Dosei | Earth | Center | {{ill|Tai Chi|ja|太極}} | style="background:yellow;"| Yellow |- ! {{ill|Sixth White Metal Star|ja|六白金星}} | Roppaku Kinsei | Metal | Northwest | {{ill|Qian|ja|乾}} | style="background:white;"| White |- ! {{ill|Seventh Red Metal Star|ja|七赤金星}} | Shichiseki Kinsei | Metal | {{ill|West|ja|西}} | {{ill|Dui|ja|兌}} | style="background:red;color:white;"| Red |- ! {{ill|Eighth White Earth Star|ja|八白土星}} | Happaku Dosei | Earth | Northeast | {{ill|Gen|ja|艮}} | style="background:white;"| White |- ! {{ill|Ninth Purple Fire Star|ja|九紫火星}} | Kyūshi Kasei | Fire | {{ill|South|ja|南}} | {{ill|Li|ja|離}} | style="background:purple;color:white;"| Purple |}
Despite their names, the Nine Stars are not related to celestial objects like the planets in the {{ill|Solar System|ja|太陽系}}.
== Relationships Among the Stars == The relationships among the Nine Stars follow the {{ill|five elements theory|ja|五行思想}}:
{| class="wikitable" |- ! Star ! Beneficial (Compatible) ! Neutral (Compatible) ! Harmful (Incompatible) |- ! First White Water Star | Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star, Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star | First White Water Star | Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Eighth White Earth Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star |- ! Second Black Earth Star | Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star | Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Eighth White Earth Star | First White Water Star, Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star |- ! Third Blue Wood Star | First White Water Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star | Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star | Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star, Eighth White Earth Star |- ! Fourth Green Wood Star | First White Water Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star | Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star | Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star, Eighth White Earth Star |- ! Fifth Yellow Earth Star | Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star | Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Eighth White Earth Star | First White Water Star, Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star |- ! Sixth White Metal Star | First White Water Star, Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Eighth White Earth Star | Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star | Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star |- ! Seventh Red Metal Star | First White Water Star, Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Eighth White Earth Star | Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star | Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star |- ! Eighth White Earth Star | Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star | Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Eighth White Earth Star | First White Water Star, Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star |- ! Ninth Purple Fire Star | Second Black Earth Star, Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Eighth White Earth Star | Ninth Purple Fire Star | First White Water Star, Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star |}
These relationships are used for predicting {{ill|compatibility|ja|相性}}, {{ill|fortune|ja|運勢}}, and {{ill|auspicious directions|ja|吉方位}}.

{{otheruses|Nine Stars of Divination|Nine Stars in Indian Astronomy|Nine Luminaries]] {{Cite source|date=December 2018]] {| class="wikitable" |- | {{ill|Kun|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:坤]] |- | {{ill|Zhen|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:震]] |- | {{ill|Xun|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:巽]] |- | {{ill|Tai Chi|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:太極]] |- | {{ill|Qian|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:乾]] |- | {{ill|Dui|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:兌]] |- | {{ill|Gen|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:艮]] |- | {{ill|Li|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:離]] |}{{color]] '''Nine Stars''' ({{ill|Nine Stars|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:九星]], Kyūsei) is a form of [[folk belief]] originating from ancient [[China]], consisting of nine stars: '''First White''', '''Second Black''', '''Third Blue''', '''Fourth Green''', '''Fifth Yellow''', '''Sixth White''', '''Seventh Red''', '''Eighth White''', and '''Ninth Purple'''.
The term "Nine Stars" can refer to several systems, and the one described here is specifically referred to as the "Purple White Nine Stars" or "Seven Colored Stars."
== Origin == The Nine Stars system originates from the following {{ill|magic square|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:魔方陣]]:
{| class="wikitable" |- |Four||Nine||Two |- |Three||Five||Seven |- |Eight||One||Six |}
In this magic square, the sum of any row, column, or diagonal equals 15. It uses the numbers 1 through 9 exactly once in a 3×3 grid. This configuration, called the '''Later Heaven Arrangement''' ({{ill|Later Heaven Arrangement|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:後天定位盤]]), is the only one of its kind, excluding rotations and reflections. These numbers are paired with seven colors (white, black, blue, green, yellow, red, and purple), the {{ill|five elements|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:五行思想]] ({{ill|wood|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:木]], {{ill|fire|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:火]], {{ill|earth|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:土]], {{ill|metal|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:金]], and {{ill|water|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:水]]), the {{ill|ten heavenly stems|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:十干]], the {{ill|twelve earthly branches|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:十二支]], and the {{ill|eight trigrams|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:八卦]] of {{ill|I Ching|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:易経]]. When these numbers shift positions, interpretations are added to form the "Nine Stars."
According to legend, {{ill|Yu the Great|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:禹]], founder of the {{ill|Xia Dynasty|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:夏王朝]], conceived this magic square when he encountered a sacred turtle emerging from the {{ill|Luo River|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:洛水]]. This magic square is called the "Writing of the Luo" ({{ill|Luo Writing|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:洛書]]), one of the {{ill|River Chart and Luo Writing|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:河図洛書]].

{{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}} '''Kon''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wu Xing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan (☵)|ja|坎}}, {{ill|Gen (☶)|ja|艮}}, {{ill|Zhen (☳)|ja|震}}, {{ill|Xun (☴)|ja|巽}}, {{ill|Li (☲)|ja|離}}, Kon (坤), {{ill|Dui (☱)|ja|兌}}, and {{ill|Qian (☰)|ja|乾}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kon''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wu Xing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan (☵)|ja|坎}}, {{ill|Gen (☶)|ja|艮}}, {{ill|Zhen (☳)|ja|震}}, {{ill|Xun (☴)|ja|巽}}, {{ill|Li (☲)|ja|離}}, Kon (坤), {{ill|Dui (☱)|ja|兌}}, and {{ill|Qian (☰)|ja|乾}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kon''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan (☵)|ja|坎}}, {{ill|Gen (☶)|ja|艮}}, {{ill|Zhen (☳)|ja|震}}, {{ill|Xun (☴)|ja|巽}}, {{ill|Li (☲)|ja|離}}, Kon (坤), {{ill|Dui (☱)|ja|兌}}, and {{ill|Qian (☰)|ja|乾}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kon''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kon''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kon''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:坤]]

{{Bagua}} '''Kon''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:坤]]

[[fr:K%C5%ABn (symbole asiatique)]]

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:坤]]

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:坤]]

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:坤]]

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.

Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:坤]]

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kon below and Kon above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kon symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kon is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kon corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kon corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kon is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. {{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kun below and Kun above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kun symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kun is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kun corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kun corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kun is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kun below and Kun above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kun symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kun is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kun corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kun corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kun is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kun below and Kun above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kun symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.

Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kun below and Kun above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kun symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kun is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kun corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kun corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kun is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kun below and Kun above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kun symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kun is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kun corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kun corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kun is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:坤]]

revision.text:
{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kun below and Kun above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kun symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kun is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kun corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kun corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kun is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:坤]]

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地}}, consisting of Kun below and Kun above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kun symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Kun is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Kun corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kun corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Kun is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位|12=draft|12=draft}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南|12=draft|12=draft}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲|12=draft|12=draft}} system, Kun is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東|12=draft|12=draft}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方|12=draft|12=draft}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北|12=draft|12=draft}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位|12=draft|12=draft}}, Kun corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南|12=draft|12=draft}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支|12=draft|12=draft}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)|12=draft|12=draft}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kun corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申|12=draft|12=draft}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦|12=draft|12=draft}}, Kun is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北|12=draft|12=draft}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

{{Bagua}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦|12=draft|12=draft}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦|12=draft|12=draft}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地|12=draft|12=draft}}, consisting of Kun below and Kun above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kun symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位|12=draft|12=draft}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南|12=draft|12=draft}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲|12=draft|12=draft}} system, Kun is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東|12=draft|12=draft}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方|12=draft|12=draft}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北|12=draft|12=draft}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位|12=draft|12=draft}}, Kun corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南|12=draft|12=draft}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支|12=draft|12=draft}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt=Dui (☱)|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)|12=draft|12=draft}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kun corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申|12=draft|12=draft}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦|12=draft|12=draft}}, Kun is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北|12=draft|12=draft}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.

revision.text:
{{八卦}} '''坤'''（こん）は[[八卦]]の一つ。卦の形は{{resize|125%|'''☷'''}}であり、三[[爻]]すべてが[[陰陽|陰]]で構成される。または[[六十四卦]]の一つであり、[[周易上経三十卦の一覧#坤|坤為地]]。坤下坤上で構成される。
== 卦象 == 地・順・牛・腹・母・祖母・婦徳・胃・右肩・腹・補佐役・鈍重・大衆・迷いなどを象徴する。[[方位]]としては[[西南]]を示す。
[[納甲]]では[[乙]]、[[五行思想|五行]]の[[木]]、[[五方]]の[[東]]、または[[癸]]、[[五行思想|五行]]の[[水]]、[[五方]]の[[北]]に当てられる。
== 方角 == [[方位]]としては[[西南]]になる。全方位（東西南北）を十二支で12等分した場合、北東、東南、南西、西北が表現できないため、これと別に北から時計回りに坎（かん）、艮（ごん）、震（しん）、巽（そん）、離（り）、坤（こん）、兌（だ）、乾（けん）の八卦を使って方角を表現した<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」国立国会図書館 2021年12月16日閲覧</ref>。[[地支]]の[[未]]と[[申]]の間、'''ひつじさる'''を示す。
== 先天図 == 伏羲先天八卦における次序は八であり、方位は四正卦の一つで[[北]]に配される。[[陰陽]]消息は陰が極まったところである。

{{Bagua|qq=}} '''Kun''' (坤) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bagua|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bagua|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bagua|qq=}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☷'''|qq=}} and consists of three Yin (⚋) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao (lines)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao (lines)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao (lines)|qq=}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixty-Four Hexagrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixty-Four Hexagrams|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixty-Four Hexagrams|qq=}}, known as {{ill|Kun as Earth|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun為地|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun as Earth|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun as Earth|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun as Earth|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}}, consisting of Kun below and Kun above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Kun symbolizes earth, compliance, cattle, the abdomen, the mother, grandmother, feminine virtues, the stomach, the right shoulder, support roles, sluggishness, the masses, and hesitation. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cardinal direction|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cardinal direction|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cardinal direction|qq=}}, it represents {{ill|southwest|ja|西南|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/southwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/southwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/southwest|qq=}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Na Jia|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Na Jia|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Na Jia|qq=}} system, Kun is associated with {{ill|Yi (Heavenly Stem)|ja|乙|1=Kinoto (乙)|lt=Kinoto (乙)|2=ja|3=乙|4=zh|5=乙|1=Kinoto (乙)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yi (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinoto (乙)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yi (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinoto (乙)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yi (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinoto (乙)|qq=}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|2=ja|3=五行思想|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|13=User:Immanuelle/Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qq=}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/east|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/east|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/east|qq=}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方|lt=Five Directions|1=Cardinal direction|2=ja|3=方位|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Directions|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Directions|13=User:Immanuelle/Cardinal direction|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Directions|13=User:Immanuelle/Cardinal direction|qq=}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Gui (Heavenly Stem)|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)|lt=Mizunoto (癸)|2=ja|3=癸|4=zh|5=癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gui (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizunoto (癸)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gui (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizunoto (癸)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gui (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizunoto (癸)|qq=}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/north|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/north|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/north|qq=}}.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cardinal direction|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cardinal direction|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cardinal direction|qq=}}, Kun corresponds to the {{ill|southwest|ja|西南|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/southwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/southwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/southwest|qq=}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Branches|qq=}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坎|lt=Kan (坎)|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|Kan=c|lt=Kan (☵)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt\=Gen (☶)|lt=Gen (☶)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhen (震)|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun|13=User:Immanuelle/Xun (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|2=ja|3=離|lt=Li (離)|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Li|13=User:Immanuelle/Li (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Li|13=User:Immanuelle/Li (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Li|13=User:Immanuelle/Li (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坤|lt=Kun (坤)|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui (Bagua)|qq=}}, and {{ill|Qian|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian|lt=Qian (☰)|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian (Bagua)|qq=}}—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Kun corresponds to the area between {{ill|Wei (Earthly Branch)|ja|未|1=Goat (Zodiac)|lt=Goat (未)|2=ja|3=未|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wei (Earthly Branch)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wei (Earthly Branch)|13=User:Immanuelle/Goat (Zodiac)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wei (Earthly Branch)|13=User:Immanuelle/Goat (Zodiac)|qq=}} and {{ill|Shen (Earthly Branch)|ja|申|1=Monkey (Zodiac)|lt=Monkey (申)|2=ja|3=申|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shen (Earthly Branch)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shen (Earthly Branch)|13=User:Immanuelle/Monkey (Zodiac)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shen (Earthly Branch)|13=User:Immanuelle/Monkey (Zodiac)|qq=}}, known as *Hitsujisaru* (ひつじさる).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|qq=}}, Kun is the eighth in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|north|ja|北|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/north|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/north|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/north|qq=}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yin.
